Task: Sanitize PyYAML constructor failures in load_config
Description: config.load_config catches only yaml.YAMLError, but PyYAML's construction stage raises whatever Python raised at it: an out-of-range implicit timestamp (2026-02-30) raises ValueError, !!bool <junk> raises KeyError(<the value>), !!timestamp <junk> raises AttributeError, and deep flow nesting raises RecursionError. Two of those put file content in the message, so a secret pasted into config.yaml reaches the terminal in an unhandled traceback. Same defect and same fix as the one closed in research/allowlist.py at M1-308 round 7; found there, filed here because it is pre-existing on the diff base.
Acceptance Criteria: load_config translates every non-YAMLError failure of yaml.safe_load into a sanitized ConfigError raised from None; no value from the file appears in the message or the cause chain; regression tests cover the invalid implicit timestamp, the !!bool/!!int/!!timestamp explicit-tag shapes and deep flow nesting.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-308 round-7 review; CLAUDE.md error hygiene

Task: Gut the questions package __init__ re-export block
Description: questions/__init__.py re-exports every submodule, so importing whiskeyjack_bot.questions.model -- the canonical question schema, which imports no SDK itself -- transitively loads forecasting_tools, asknews_sdk, litellm, httpx and streamlit. Pre-existing on master with no live symptom today (env_verify and cli import no canonical question, and test_env_verify.py's subprocess probe fails if that changes). Found while building M1-402, whose forecast/inputs.py inherits the coupling and documents it rather than fixing a merged module on a review branch.
Acceptance Criteria: questions/__init__.py holds a one-line docstring and no re-exports; a fresh interpreter importing whiskeyjack_bot.questions.model loads none of forecasting_tools, asknews_sdk, litellm, httpx or streamlit; every existing importer of the removed names is updated to the submodule path; the four gates stay green.

Task: Decide the terminal DNS root dot in canonicalize_url

Task: Compose artifact and ledger persistence for a paid run
Description: research.store and research.artifacts are separate primitives, so the ordering rule that keeps a paid run recordable when its artifact write fails - write the artifact first, then persist the ledger row with raw_response_path NULL - lives only in a docstring and in the caller. M1-306 deliberately shipped the primitives without the composition, because the composed entry point belongs with the retrieval orchestrator that item does not ship.
Acceptance Criteria: One paid-result persistence API attempts artifact storage and still commits the run and its documents with raw_response_path NULL after an ordinary artifact I/O failure, and reports the audit loss to its caller rather than swallowing it.

Description: ResearchPacket is a frozen dataclass holding tuples of pydantic models, so its digest is stable against rebinding its fields but not against mutating a caller-retained run, document, query list or provider-config dict after build_packet returns. Acceptance Criteria: After build_packet returns, mutation of caller-owned runs, documents, lists or provider-config dictionaries cannot change the packet's digest; a property test asserts the digest is unchanged after mutating each mutable input.

Task: Cross-check the configured probability bounds against the prompt
Description: forecast.min_probability and forecast.max_probability are enforced against model output by M1-403, while prompts/forecaster.md prints 0.001-0.999 to the model as a literal. Nothing compares the two, so narrowing the config silently asks for a probability the prompt never permits and pays for a repair turn to discover it. M1-403 made the divergence observable rather than creating it, so it is a row and not a fix on that branch.
Acceptance Criteria: A config whose probability bounds fall outside the range the loaded prompt declares is reported at startup and by verify-env, before any billable call; the check reads the prompt that config actually names rather than a copy of its numbers.

Task: Enforce the prompt's evidence caps against document provenance
Description: prompts/forecaster.md caps what a document may justify by its reliability_tag and provenance: an unverified_social document "may justify a tiny or small adjustment at most, never a load-bearing fact", and an llm_reported one is capped at small unless the cited account is official_primary or a direct_api document corroborates it. The response schema carries direction, magnitude and load_bearing, and M1-501 resolves every citation to a supplied source_id -- but a source_id is only an identity, so nothing compares a claimed magnitude against the reliability of the document it cites. A forecast can still rest a load-bearing fact on a single unverified social post and be recorded as valid. Enforcing the caps needs the documents themselves (ForecastDocumentInput.reliability_tag/provenance), not just their ids, which is a wider input than M1-501's checker takes and a rule the prompt states rather than one this project would be inventing. Raised while implementing M1-501.
Acceptance Criteria: An evidence adjustment or load-bearing fact whose citations are all documents the prompt caps below the claimed magnitude is refused as a repairable sanitized problem before the forecast is recorded; a corroborating direct_api citation lifts the llm_reported cap exactly as the prompt states, and no message echoes document content.

Task: Expose one composed output-validation entry point
Description: The output checks a valid forecast must pass are split across modules on purpose -- attribution.attribution_problems (cross-type, M1-501), binary.binary_output_problems (M1-403), and the option-set and percentile-level checks M1-404 and M1-405 will add. generate._output_problems composes them, but it is private to the call path, so a caller that is NOT generating -- M1-406 replaying a stored response, M1-602 validating a record before it is persisted -- has to know the full list and call each one. Nothing tells it when that list grows. M1-501's round-1 cross-model review reported a missing binary-prior check against attribution.py for exactly this reason: reading one checker in isolation, the rule looks absent. The rule was present in binary.py and the composed path refuses the response (reproduced by execution, rebutted in round 2), but a seam that misleads a careful reader is a seam a caller will get wrong.
Acceptance Criteria: One public entry point returns every output problem for a response of any supported question type, composing the cross-type and type-specific checkers; generate._output_problems is defined in terms of it rather than beside it, so the two cannot diverge; a test fails if a supported question type has a checker the entry point does not reach.

Task: Apply the non-blank identifier guard to the pre-004 identifier columns
Description: Migration 004 and lifecycle._require_identifier refuse a blank or blob attempt_id on both ends of the attempt->forecast join. The identifier columns that shipped before it -- forecast_records.record_id, submission_attempts.attempt_id and idempotency_key, research_runs.retrieval_run_id -- have no such guard: _require_text refuses '' but '\n\t' is truthy and reaches storage, and one-argument trim() in 001/003 strips U+0020 alone. Pre-existing, so M1-606 scoped its fix to its own writer rather than widening a shared validator under already-reviewed code.
Acceptance Criteria: A whitespace-only or blob identifier is refused at every writer and every trigger that takes one, with the same 29-codepoint whitespace set 003 pinned; a test asserts the writer and trigger definitions agree over every codepoint Python calls whitespace.
Source or Decision Reference: D25; M1-606 M1-NOTES deviation; M1-603 round 5

Task: Pin the shared identifier bound between lifecycle and approval
Description: approval._MAX_IDENTIFIER restates lifecycle._MAX_IDENTIFIER (both 200) with no pinned relationship. approval.py deliberately does not import lifecycle's private validators -- they raise the wrong error type -- so the bound was respelled, and a future change to either constant would silently let the two entry points accept different record_id sets. Behaviour agrees at this revision, so this is a hardening item rather than a live defect.
Acceptance Criteria: Approval and lifecycle entry points derive the record_id length limit from one public contract; a test asserts the two accepted input sets cannot diverge if that limit changes.

Task: Bind an approval to the submission payload it authorized
Description: An approval binds to forecast_sha256, so one approved forecast covers every payload built from it: a payload that changed without the forecast changing gets a new idempotency key (M2-702) while keeping its old approval in force. M2-702 ships the half it can -- submission_key_for_approved_record refuses a record with no approval -- but cannot check that a payload IS the one the approval meant, because the forecast->payload mapping does not exist until M1-502/M1-503. Raised by M2-702 round-1 cross-model review; reading recorded as D33.
Acceptance Criteria: A submission payload that does not derive from the approved forecast is refused before any post; the binding is append-only and an operator can see what a decision authorized.

Task: Reserve an idempotency key atomically before any post
Description: submission.require_key_unused() is a read and says so: two concurrent commands can both see one key as unused, and 001's UNIQUE constraint only refuses the second row AFTER its post has been made. Nothing is reachable today -- no gateway exists -- but the post-call insert cannot by itself prevent a duplicate live post. Raised as a backlog candidate by M2-702 round-1 cross-model review.
Acceptance Criteria: Two concurrent commands for the same derived key durably select one poster before any network I/O; the loser posts nothing, and every completed call remains recordable.

Task: Verify SQLite foreign-key enforcement after connection setup
Description: ledger.connect sets PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON but never reads it back, unlike journal_mode and recursive_triggers, which are both read back and raise LedgerError when the setting did not take. An unknown or ignored PRAGMA is a silent no-op in SQLite, so foreign-key enforcement is assumed rather than verified. M1-607 relies on that assumption: it guards the five identifier primary keys directly and leaves every FK column (the four *_forecast_record_id columns, forecast_records/research_documents.retrieval_run_id) covered transitively. Declared there as a standing risk rather than fixed, because reading the PRAGMA back changes ledger.connect's contract and belongs to its own item. Raised as a non-blocking backlog candidate by M1-607 cross-model review round 1.
Acceptance Criteria: ledger.connect reads PRAGMA foreign_keys back and raises LedgerError unless it is enabled, with a message naming the path and no stored value; a test asserts the refusal, and the existing journal_mode/recursive_triggers read-backs are the shape to follow. Note in the item that no deterministic failure is reproducible on the supported SQLite runtime -- the PRAGMA is recognized and set outside a transaction -- so this closes an unverified assumption rather than a demonstrated defect.
Source or Decision Reference: M1-607 review round 1 (non-blocking); M1-607 M1-NOTES standing risk
